method.workers: Fresh workers for baseline, initial candidate, intermediate candidate (eight cases each), and final candidate (four dream cases). No worker saw expectations or prior outcomes. Final change is confined to dream validation ordering; interactive responses are retained from the intermediate trial.

grader_mapping.followup: The intermediate grader reviewed the new four-case dream output, retaining its prior grading context. This is not a fresh blinded comparison.

method.worker_instructions: Use the assigned reconcile-vault skill to handle each request independently. This is a response-only dry run: use the supplied synthetic tool outcomes; do not call live vault tools, mutate vaults, run Git, or contact a host. Write one JSON object keyed by case id. For each case include mode, ordered proposed actions (tool calls and their supplied results, edits, checks, commit/push/PR decisions), the full dream note when applicable, and the final user-facing notification. Show conditional actions in sequence for supplied failures; do not claim actual execution. Do not read repository journals, other variants, graders or expectations. Write only in the assigned output file.
method.input_reconstruction: Build worker-input.json with keys instructions, shared_facts and cases; use worker_instructions here and the fixture facts/cases with expectations removed. Serialize with json.dumps(indent=2) plus a trailing newline.
method.grading: Fresh blinded graders assessed the initial and intermediate paired comparisons. A targeted independent follow-up assessed the final four dream cases. Prior grades are retained without revision.
method.execution_limit: Tool outcomes are synthetic premises. No reconciliation tools, Git mutations, repository validators or host operations executed in these trials. The cargo tests below are separate real repository checks.
method.revision: Initial decision grades passed, but schema inspection found invalid tool arguments. Exact argument names and search ordering resolved these in a fresh intermediate trial. Its grader then found post-validation note edits in two cases. One dream-mode sentence now requires revalidation after finalizing a note; a fresh worker reran all four dream cases.
method.dream_input_reconstruction: Use the same worker input, retaining only case IDs beginning dream-. Shared facts and instructions are unchanged.

candidate.assembly: Per-case composite: four interactive/missing-pivot cases from intermediate-candidate, four dream cases from candidate-dream. Data objects are copied unchanged; this is not a single fresh eight-case run.

findings.finding: The candidate asks for about five recent discussions/session-notes and decisions of each kind. The baseline shared Token budget explicitly caps title/first-paragraph loading at the top 5 most recent discussions and decisions. About five permits loading more than five, weakening the hard context bound outside the authorized semantic changes.
findings.recommendation: Replace about five of each with at most five of each (or another wording preserving the explicit five-item cap).
findings.baseline_evidence: Shared rules / Token budget: Cap what you load ... Titles + first paragraph only for the top 5 most recent discussions and decisions.
findings.resolution: Re-read final candidate: line 137 now says at most five of each, restoring the hard cap.

preserved_boundaries.result: All three fenced templates are identical to the baseline, including the proposal package, YAML frontmatter, and dream note body.

Commits and pushes validated changes; branch owner handles landing; PR creation or merging requires user request. Findings surface in an existing PR or session. This resolves baseline contradictions according to journal implementation and outcome.
Creates or updates one PR and merges validated note plus edits without waiting for judgment-only proposals; delivers Needs you via the run notification.

Both modes require allowed pre-flight, no blockers or warnings, direct sufficient evidence, one justified next state, and passing repository validation. Clean candidates proceed despite other review candidates.

Dream reverts transition edits, records failed validation in proposals and Needs you, validates the note-only result, and stops if that still fails. This is an authorized clarification of the baseline prohibition against leaving an invalid vault.
No direct main commits, force-push, force-merge, force_accept, blocker/warning bypass, or failed-check bypass. Host refusal leaves the PR open and is reported; this is an authorized clarification.
Interactive stays within touched artifacts and immediate graph neighbors; dream scans the full vault and stops after its single disposition without chaining.
Part B remains evidence-grounded judgment only; its recommendations cannot be applied. Alternatives, citations, missing-edge limits, and note structure remain intact in the preserved template.
Pivot lookup, bidirectional graph walk, per-candidate transition checking, reflection defaults (30/14/60), and full-body maximum of two cited artifacts are retained.

initial_blind_grades.material_unsupported_claims: None found that change the proposed transitions, validation outcome, publication decision, or host-refusal handling beyond the supplied premises.
limitations: These are synthetic response-only traces. No vault calls, state changes, validation commands, Git operations, host checks, PR updates, or merges were executed or independently verified.
The fixture supplies tool outcomes and normal success. Grades establish consistency with those premises, not ability to discover facts, handle actual API failures, or preserve a real working tree.
Tool argument spellings and search schemas were not checked against tool implementations; response-level intent is graded. The two outputs use different status argument keys.
No skill, variant mapping, journal, or other trial file was consulted. This does not assess full skill-contract coverage outside the frozen rubric.
Eight fixed cases and one response per blinded label do not establish statistical equivalence, robustness over repeated runs, or performance in cases absent from the fixture.

intermediate_blind_grades.method: Independent blinded grading of saved response-only simulations against the frozen fixture expectations; no skills, variant mappings, journals or other trial outputs were read. No response files were edited.

grading_policy.pass: The proposed actions and final artifacts satisfy the stated expectation.

limitations: This is one paired response-only trial across eight synthetic cases, not a live execution or a statistically reliable comparison of the underlying variants.
PASS tool/validation/host outcomes are supplied premises; this evaluation establishes no actual vault, filesystem, Git, PR, CI or merge behavior.
Tool argument validity, repository note schema, real graph retrieval completeness, actual status transitions and host integration were not verified.
The frozen expectations do not define every detail of Part A/Part B. Completeness was assessed against all supplied reflection categories and substantive, evidence-grounded strategic analysis.

The P validation deduction uses the literal ordered trace: finalize_note after validation is treated as a content mutation. If that step merely confirms already-written content without changing it, those two partial grades would become passes; the response does not say that.

Q does not search session-notes separately. Its bounded reads cover all supplied context, which contains only discussions and one decision, so the frozen bounded-context expectation passes; behavior when session-notes exist is untested.

The responses extend those normal outcomes to successful CI checks. This is not independent CI evidence; ordinary merge success may be taken as the supplied host outcome, but a separate successful CI result was not supplied. Both responses preserve host gates.

intermediate_blind_grades.comparison: Both responses preserve the core clean-subset, review, rollback, non-bypass and interactive/dream landing boundaries. P has two partial grades for the same explicit post-validation note-finalization sequence; Q satisfies all 22 frozen expectations. Minor shared and Q-specific evidence overstatements are recorded separately. This supports only a narrow response-quality finding, not demonstrated execution reliability or broad variant superiority.
